checks.label: The sum of all currents entering a junction equals the sum leaving it: at every dial setting the load's arrow carries I₁ + I₂, drawn with its size and turned round when it is negative

The algebraic sum of changes in potential around any closed loop is zero: with the solved currents both walks end at 0 in all three circuits, and the grid and minus-current screens finish with both totals at 0 V

Each time a rule is applied an equation is produced, and as many independent equations as unknowns can be solved: several dial pairs bring each loop alone back to 0, but exactly one pair fits both, in all three circuits

If a current's direction is assigned wrongly it comes out negative, no harm done: with battery 2 at 4 V, I₂ = −1.5 A, its arrow is drawn turned round with its name and size, I₂: 1.5 A, and both walks still end at 0

Current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage drop across it: each drop is current × resistance, so doubling I₁ from 1 A to 2 A doubles battery 1's inside drop from 1 V to 2 V, and doubling both currents doubles the load's from 4 V to 8 V
The terminal voltage decreases as the current increases, because of the drop across the internal resistance: battery 1's 12 − 1 × I₁ falls at every step up its dial

Every worked line is right, by hand: 7 V and 6 V at 1 A and 1 A; 1 V at 3 A and 1 A; 4 V on loop 2 at 4 A and 0 A; 2 V on loop 1 at 2 A and 2 A; 3 V on loop 2 at 5 A and 0 A with the 10 V and 8 V batteries; the solves give 3 A and 1.5 A, 5 A and −1.5 A, and 4 A and 2 A; and 4 + (−1) = 3 A
Every puzzle has three answers, one of them right, and a hint of its own for each wrong one; the right pair fits both loops and each wrong pair fails at least one

The walk screen opens with the ring at loop 1's start and nothing added, then passes battery 1 (+12 V), its 1 Ω (−1 V) and the load (−4 V) to end at 7 V; a puzzle keeps its walk and its running totals back until Check; the pair puzzle keeps its grid back, and a wrong pair is walked to show which loop it fails
On the grid screen the dot first reaches 4 A and 0 A, where loop 1 ends at 0 V but loop 2 at 4 V, then the crossing at 3 A and 1.5 A, where both end at 0 V and the ring appears
Every demonstration settles within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and a puzzle's answer, Why? or wrong pick settles within 2.5 s
